headline: No school changed tier this run. UIUC's own ISSS blog (17 Nov) is the first school to spell out what it is doing during the injunction without reverting — resuming only the same narrower CPT categories it already allowed (curriculum-integral, tied to a required class, or thesis-related), with existing-approval treatment still unaddressed. Buffalo, Alabama and UT Dallas remain the only three full reversions; Columbia, U Washington, UC San Diego and Boston University continue to acknowledge the ruling without changing how CPT is processed. DHS's own CPT pages still make no mention of it. No new retroactive cancellations; Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and USF remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

tripwires.name: Federal Register rulemaking on CPT
tripwires.detail: RULING, 17 Nov 2026: US District Judge Julia Kobick (D. Mass.) granted the plaintiffs' motion for a preliminary injunction and stay of agency action in Association of American Universities et al. v. DHS, No. 1:26-cv-14520 — barring DHS from enforcing the Aug 12/24 SEVP CPT guidance, finding it likely arbitrary and capricious under the Administrative Procedure Act. Not a final ruling; DHS may appeal and has declined to comment. Three schools have fully reverted on their own pages (Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas); Columbia, U Washington, UC San Diego and Boston University continue to acknowledge the ruling without changing processing; UIUC's own 17 Nov ISSS blog, re-checked 19 Nov, instead details that it is resuming only the narrower CPT categories it already allowed (curriculum-integral, required-class, thesis-related) while the injunction stands — a middle path, not a reversion. DHS's own SEVIS Help Hub and CPT-guidance tripwire pages, re-confirmed 19 Nov, still have not been updated to reflect the ruling; a Federal Register/appeal search again found no CPT-specific rulemaking and no confirmed DHS appeal filing yet.

tripwires.name: Retroactive cancellation spreading
tripwires.detail: Still tripped, re-checked 19 Nov 00:09 UTC — no school newly moved into 'cancels' this run. Davidson, MIT, Skidmore and University of South Florida remain the only confirmed interruptions of already-granted CPT.

context: First CPT-specific litigation: on 5 Oct a coalition (AAU, Presidents' Alliance on Higher Education and Immigration, NAFSA, AICUM) sued DHS in federal court in Massachusetts over the Aug 12/24 BCMs, calling them procedurally invalid and impermissibly retroactive; case is Association of American Universities et al. v. U.S. Department of Homeland Security et al., No. 1:26-cv-14520 (D. Mass.). After a 6 Nov hearing, US District Judge Julia Kobick ruled 17 Nov 2026, granting a preliminary injunction and stay of agency action barring DHS from enforcing the Aug 12/24 BCMs as likely arbitrary and capricious under the APA. Not a final ruling; DHS may appeal and has declined to comment. Schools are reacting unevenly to the ruling rather than uniformly reverting — three (Buffalo, Alabama, UT Dallas) have fully reverted to pre-August standards on their own pages as of 18 Nov, several more (U Washington, UC San Diego, Boston University, and now Columbia) are reviewing or have only acknowledged the ruling with no change yet, and most official pages checked so far (DHS's own tripwire pages included) have not yet been updated to reflect it. No third broadcast message. DHS's prior stated position: 'nothing about these regulations has changed.' ICE is auditing schools, with SEVP decertification as the stated risk. Immigration attorneys flag a retroactive-scrutiny risk — past CPT revisited at the OPT, STEM-OPT or H-1B stage. The common institutional reading of the pre-injunction standard: integral to the curriculum, required of all students in the programme for degree completion, a documented cooperative agreement with the employer, and DSO authorisation before training begins.

runs.summary: No school changed tier. UIUC's own ISSS blog (17 Nov post) is the first school to detail what it's doing during the injunction without reverting: resuming only the narrower CPT categories it already allowed (curriculum-integral, required class, thesis-related); existing-approval treatment still not addressed. Rotation re-verified FIU, La Verne, Cal State Fullerton (direct fetch recovered after a durable 503 since 25 Oct) and Ohio State — all unchanged, no ruling mention. DHS and Tufts tripwires, and Claremont McKenna, unchanged; no confirmed DHS appeal or CPT Federal Register rulemaking. No new cancellations.

No school changed tier. Columbia's own 17 Nov ISSO post acknowledges the 17 Nov injunction but says ISSO is only 'preparing guidance' on what it means — no change yet, joining U Washington, UC San Diego and Boston University in that cautious posture. Rotation re-verified Brown, Northwestern, Boston College and UConn — all unchanged, no ruling mention on any of their own pages. DHS and Tufts tripwires, and Claremont McKenna, unchanged; no confirmed DHS appeal or CPT Federal Register rulemaking. No new cancellations.

A third school fully reverted post-injunction: UT Dallas's own 17 Nov ISSO post says the ruling lets it resume CPT processing under pre-August policies (moved to clear, joining Buffalo and Alabama); students with an active offer denied earlier may resubmit for re-evaluation. Other schools are more cautious: U Washington and UC San Diego say they're reviewing with no changes yet; Boston University says the relief is preliminary and doesn't change its processing. DHS and Tufts tripwires, and Claremont McKenna, unchanged. No new cancellations, no appeal confirmed yet.

A second school reacted to the 17 Nov injunction: University of Alabama's own ISSS page, recovered after a durable 503 since 6 Nov, cites the ruling and says it will resume CPT processing under standard federal regulations (moved to clear, joining U Buffalo); temporariness and treatment of prior CPT not addressed. Rotation re-verified Yale, Illinois State and (via snippet, direct fetch 503'd) UT Dallas — unchanged. DHS and Tufts tripwires, and Claremont McKenna, unchanged. No new cancellations.

DHS's own CPT pages not yet updated. No new cancellations.
